chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fudayl ibn Abu Qurra, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man, and I was present, so he said: 'What has withheld him from the Hajj?' It was said, 'He left trade and his wealth became scarce.' He said, 'And he was leaning, so he sat upright, then said to them: Do not leave trade, lest you be belittled. Trade, may Allah bless you.'

key_terms.فَتَهُونُوا: Lest you be belittled or diminished

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam advise against leaving trade in relation to performing Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual and material necessity of trade, noting that neglecting commerce leads to poverty and a diminished standing. He encourages believers to actively engage in business as a means of securing sustenance, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that lawful economic activity is a form of worship and a prerequisite for fulfilling religious obligations like Hajj. This narrative underscores the integration of worldly livelihood with spiritual duty, rejecting ascetic withdrawal from economic life.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Shareef Bin Sabiq, from Al Fuzayl Bin Abu Qurra who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man and I was present, so he<sup>asws</sup> said:’ And what has withheld him from the Hajj’. So it was said, ‘Neglect of the business and scarcity of his assets’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was leaning, so he<sup>asws</sup> sat upright then said to them: ‘Do not leave the business for you would be belittled. Do business, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you all’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq from al-Fudayl ibn abu Qurrah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked about a man, when I was present, ‘What is holding him back from performing Hajj?’ It was said, ’He has quit business and his wealth is reduced.’ He (the narrator) has said, that he (the Imam) was leaning and he moved to a straight sitting position, and said, to them, ‘You must not quit doing business to become humiliated. Do business, I pray to Allah to grant you blessings.’”
